scope: Manual encounter-by-encounter closure records for every real Verdant trainer battle, including optional routes, story encounters, gym trainers, bosses, rematches, and postgame. Mutually exclusive trainer definitions are grouped only when they are branches of one physical encounter.

BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.player_state: One starter chosen from seven regional trios. Oldale's Center teacher, ability menu, Mart core held items, $25,000 starting money, and $1,000 ten-level Rare Candy are all available.

competitive_references.adaptation: The Marshtomp donor supports the rival's simple STAB-plus-coverage identity, but the first fight deliberately avoids importing a full ladder set.
The Treecko donor confirms that early unevolved starters can sustain real competitive pressure without turning the opening into a forced sequence.

BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.team_intent: The rival always fields the type-counter starter from the same regional trio the player chose. It is level 15, one above the strict cap, with perfect IVs, a Life Orb, its universal Pledge STAB, Return, Toxic, and Protect.
BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.intended_counterplay: There is no single required solution. The player can use any legal coverage or status plan their chosen starter supports, or lean on Focus Sash, Eviolite, Leftovers, Life Orb, or a Choice item from Oldale. Protect, setup, Counter or Mirror Coat, Endeavor, speed control, and direct offense are all viable on different starters.
BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.bespoke_ai: The normal foe-aware viability AI chooses among offense, Toxic, and Protect. No opening is forced and no hidden lock-and-key sequence is required.
BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.uniqueness: The encounter supports all 21 starters across Generations 1-7 through one native counterpart rule, while May and Brendan remain mechanically identical. It introduces Verdant's preparation freedom without pretending the player already owns a full team.
BATTLE_001_ROUTE_103_RIVAL.closure: Battle 1 is a dangerous but open-ended first preparation check: the rival's exact counterpart matches the player's chosen generation, its +1 level and competitive item establish Verdant's 7.5 floor, and multiple legal plans can still win without a starter-specific lock.

registered_showcases: Mew is the deliberate rare single-stage reveal.

full_team_candidates.decision: individual set selected
full_team_candidates.reason: The full generated team has no Route 102 identity, but its Zorua is an exact fit for the false-Mew lead.

full_team_candidates.decision: support shell selected
full_team_candidates.reason: The full team is not imported; Smeargle's redirection shell is adapted specifically to enable Calvin's Mew.

corpus_review.decision: No full random or sample team is copied verbatim. Three sourced sets are integrated into one route-specific Illusion plan, with Jigglypuff supplying the missing speed and partner support.

competitive_references.adaptation: Zorua's Expert Belt, Illusion, Hidden Power Fighting, Dark Pulse, Extrasensory, and Sucker Punch set is imported verbatim as the deceptive lead.
Smeargle keeps the donor's Fake Out, Helping Hand, and Follow Me support shell; Focus Sash plus Endeavor replaces King's Shield so it cannot become a harmless final slot.
Mew's Sitrus Berry, Psyshock, Nasty Plot, Aura Sphere, and Will-O-Wisp set is imported as the real late-game ace.
The bulky Jigglypuff support donor is rebuilt for active doubles tempo with Friend Guard, Icy Wind, Helping Hand, Dazzling Gleam, and Protect.

BATTLE_002_ROUTE_102_CALVIN.team_intent: Zorua leads beside Friend Guard Jigglypuff while Illusion makes it appear to be the Mew held in the final slot. Icy Wind and Helping Hand turn the false Mew into immediate pressure; Focus Sash Smeargle then creates a redirection or Fake Out window for the real Mew to use Nasty Plot and clean.
BATTLE_002_ROUTE_102_CALVIN.intended_counterplay: This team has several answers rather than one key. Spread attacks expose Illusion and bypass Follow Me, Taunt shuts down Jigglypuff or Smeargle, priority finishes a Sash-broken Smeargle, and early Bug, Ghost, and Dark options pressure Mew. The player can also double-target the support slot, contest speed with their own Icy Wind or Electroweb, or overwhelm the frail Zorua lead.
BATTLE_002_ROUTE_102_CALVIN.bespoke_ai: Calvin uses normal foe-aware doubles scoring plus partner support, speed-control preference, and smart switching. No move or turn is forced; the sets are deliberately legible to the general AI.
BATTLE_002_ROUTE_102_CALVIN.uniqueness: This is Calvin's playground illusion team: the first apparent Mew is a local Zorua, the second is real, and Smeargle plus Jigglypuff make the deception function as a complete four-Pokémon plan. No later encounter will reuse this false-ace structure.
BATTLE_002_ROUTE_102_CALVIN.closure: Battle 2 is the first full-team doubles exam. It is difficult because the player must identify the false Mew, manage active speed and partner support, and preserve an answer for a level-15 Nasty Plot Mew—not because the battle demands one preselected counter.

BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.player_state: The player can bring six level-14 Pokémon from Routes 101, 102, and 103 plus Old Rod encounters, with every legal move, ability switching, and the core held-item shop.

evolution_stage_fit.reason: Dewpider evolves at 22, Anorith at 40, Karrablast through its Shelmet trade interaction, and Larvesta at 49; all four are legitimately young at their authored levels.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Galvantula supplies an attacking Sticky Web lead model, but the surrounding Altaria, Poliwrath, Sceptile, Dusknoir, and Persian form an unrelated mature singles team.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Armaldo provides the correct Rock-and-Bug retaliation shell, but the complete doubles team does not fit a young Route 102 Bug Catcher and the evolved fossil itself belongs later.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Escavalier's Megahorn and Swords Dance role is ideal inspiration, but its five partners and mature final form do not belong in the cap-14 chapter.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Life Orb Volcarona demonstrates late Fire/Bug pressure, but Quiver Dance and the final form are deliberately replaced by a recoil-limited juvenile Larvesta pivot.

corpus_review.decision: All 983 teams were reviewed, and none contains any exact proposed four-species overlap because competitive corpora rarely use these first stages. Rick therefore adapts four mature competitive roles to stage-legal youngsters instead of pretending a verbatim tournament team belongs at cap 14.

competitive_references.adaptation: Dewpider translates Galvantula's attacking Web lead into a legal juvenile: Focus Sash preserves one action, while Water Bubble Scald plus Ice Beam and Giga Drain prevent the lead from becoming dead weight.

Anorith inherits Armaldo's X-Scissor and Rock Slide coverage; Choice Band, Aqua Jet, and Knock Off make the unevolved fossil an immediate anti-Fire and anti-Flying breaker rather than another setup slot.
Karrablast receives Escavalier's Megahorn and Swords Dance identity. Eviolite and No Guard support legal Drill Run and Knock Off, leaving it as the team's single setup win condition.

The mature Volcarona donor is not copied. Larvesta keeps only its Life Orb Fire/Bug pressure and uses legal Flare Blitz, U-turn, Wild Charge, and Morning Sun so recoil and imperfect coverage keep the level-16 ace answerable.

BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.team_intent: Focus Sash Water Bubble Dewpider establishes Sticky Web while threatening real special coverage. Choice Band Anorith immediately punishes the Fire and Flying attacks invited by the Bug theme, Eviolite No Guard Karrablast is the only setup threat, and level-16 Life Orb Larvesta closes through recoil-limited physical pressure and U-turn rather than a mature Quiver Dance sweep.
BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.intended_counterplay: Taunt, multihit attacks, or immediate pressure can deny Web; Flying and Levitate Pokémon ignore it, and legal removal clears it. Wingull, Shinx, Blitzle, Rotom, Bonsly, Rock coverage, priority, and faster Choice users are already available. Intimidate, burns, and physical walls constrain the three backliners, while Water and Rock pressure force Larvesta to spend recoil or recovery turns. No one counter is required.
BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.bespoke_ai: Rick remains an intentional singles pacing fight. First-turn setup preference makes Sticky Web or Karrablast's Swords Dance worth considering, while smart switching and normal foe-aware scoring preserve attacks, Choice locking, recovery, and pivots. No move or opening is forced.
BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.uniqueness: This is Verdant's juvenile Bug Web lesson: all four species are first-stage, Anorith and Karrablast appear on no other current trainer, Dewpider appears only in mutually exclusive later rival branches, and Larvesta's other uses are substantially later. The mature Leavanny/Scizor/Heracross/Frosmoth version is preserved for a cap-55 Bug specialist.
BATTLE_003_ROUTE_102_RICK.closure: Battle 3 is 10/10 because it proves unevolved Pokémon can support a real competitive hazard plan. Web feeds three distinct physical tempos, but the team has one Sash, one setup slot, exploitable shared weaknesses, recoil, a Choice lock, and several independent forms of counterplay.

full_team_candidates.reason: Taillow appears beside Zapdos, Spiritomb, Luxray, Snubbull, and Cacturne in the wrong battle format. Only its exact Guts cleaner set fits Allen.

corpus_review.decision: No complete team contains more than one of these four Pokémon. Four competitive roles are integrated into one 'beginner Pokémon, expert doubles' battle with three first-stage members, one young mascot exception, one setup move, and no guaranteed redirection Sash.

competitive_references.adaptation: Zigzagoon keeps Quick Feet, Belly Drum, Extreme Speed, and Seed Bomb; Sitrus Berry plus Protect replaces Leftovers plus Substitute so the doubles setup is powerful but interactable.

Parasect's Dry Skin, Spore, Protect, Seed Bomb, and Rage Powder shell is moved down to level-15 Paras. Eviolite replaces Sitrus Berry so the first-stage supporter remains useful without pretending it already evolved at level 24.

Taillow's Toxic Orb, Guts, Protect, Quick Attack, Brave Bird, and Facade set is imported verbatim as the level-15 closer.

BATTLE_004_ROUTE_102_ALLEN.team_intent: Light Ball Lightning Rod Pikachu and Toxic Orb Guts Taillow lead with Fake Out, Electroweb speed control, priority, immediate damage, and protection from Electric targeting. Eviolite Dry Skin Paras and Sitrus Quick Feet Zigzagoon form the back-line setup mode: Rage Powder or Spore can buy Belly Drum, then Extreme Speed supplies pressure.
BATTLE_004_ROUTE_102_ALLEN.intended_counterplay: The opening pair is vulnerable to Ground, Rock, Intimidate, and coordinated targeting; Protect can also expose Fake Out or consume Taillow's first Guts turn. When the back line appears, Fake Out, Taunt, spread damage, early Grass or Overcoat Pokémon, Hatenna's Magic Bounce, Fire or Flying pressure, or a double target can remove the frail Eviolite Paras before it buys a free Drum. Dreepy, Rotom, and other Ghosts ignore Extreme Speed and Facade, while Intimidate and burns hinder Zigzagoon. The player can disrupt either wave without predicting a forced opening.
BATTLE_004_ROUTE_102_ALLEN.bespoke_ai: Allen uses normal foe-aware doubles scoring plus partner awareness and contextual speed control. The AI can choose immediate Pikachu and Taillow pressure before the later redirection option appears; Rage Powder, Spore, Belly Drum, Fake Out, Electroweb, Protect, and attacks are evaluated normally, with no forced move, target, turn, or switch.
BATTLE_004_ROUTE_102_ALLEN.uniqueness: Allen weaponizes three true first-stage Pokémon and one young mascot through real doubles roles: Light Ball Pikachu, Guts Taillow, Eviolite redirection Paras, and Belly Drum Zigzagoon. Leading with offense keeps the later Rage Powder setup from repeating Calvin's opening redirection pattern. Wally's current Mauville redirection-plus-Belly Drum module is explicitly flagged for replacement when that encounter is audited.
BATTLE_004_ROUTE_102_ALLEN.closure: Battle 4 is difficult because either two-Pokémon wave can snowball, but neither begins behind guaranteed redirection and every enabling action has several legal interruptions. It now demonstrates the intended progression rule directly: young Pokémon can execute expert doubles without being replaced by premature evolved forms.

full_team_candidates.reason: Slush Rush Arctozolt is the right single-stage payoff, but Alolan Ninetales and the mature OU shell are tabled for a later snow specialist.

corpus_review.decision: No complete youthful snow team fits verbatim. Four mature competitive roles are translated into three first-stage Pokémon and one single-stage fossil, with one setup axis and no premature final evolution.

competitive_references.adaptation: Amaura inherits Aurorus's Focus Sash, Snow Warning, Aurora Veil, Blizzard, and Earth Power shell. Protect replaces Stealth Rock for a fragile doubles lead.

Alolan Sandshrew keeps Sandslash's Slush Rush and Iron Head identity. Eviolite, Icicle Crash, Brick Break, and Rapid Spin create immediate juvenile pressure and an active answer to the player's field setup without importing Swords Dance.
Swinub's corpus set already supplies Icicle Crash and Superpower. Choice Band, Ice Shard, and Rock Slide turn it into a no-setup priority and spread attacker.

BATTLE_005_ROUTE_102_TIANA.team_intent: Focus Sash Snow Warning Amaura and Eviolite Slush Rush Alolan Sandshrew lead with Aurora Veil, accurate Blizzard, fast Ice and Steel pressure, and Brick Break utility. Choice Band Thick Fat Swinub adds Ice Shard priority, Rock Slide spread damage, and Superpower, while level-16 Expert Belt Slush Rush Arctozolt is the single-stage Bolt Beak ace.
BATTLE_005_ROUTE_102_TIANA.intended_counterplay: Remove or replace snow, Taunt or double-target Sash Amaura before Veil, break Veil, or use Wide Guard against Blizzard and Rock Slide. Fire, Fighting, Rock, Steel, Ground, and Water coverage hit different members; Flying and Levitate avoid Ground coverage, priority and Trick Room bypass Slush Rush, and Intimidate or burns contain all three physical attackers. Protect punishes Bolt Beak timing, and the team has no second setup mode once Veil is denied.
BATTLE_005_ROUTE_102_TIANA.bespoke_ai: Tiana uses foe-aware smart switching plus field-control and first-turn setup preferences. Snow is automatic; Aurora Veil receives a contextual bonus without being forced, and the now-irrelevant generic speed-control profile is removed because no team member uses an active speed-control move.
BATTLE_005_ROUTE_102_TIANA.uniqueness: This is Verdant's first full weather battle and its juvenile fossil snow lesson. Amaura and Alolan Sandshrew appear on no other current trainer, Swinub's only other use is a much later level-one gimmick, and no Battles 1-4 species repeats. The mature Ninetales-A/Froslass/Mamoswine shell is preserved for cap-70 Route 133 trainer Linda.
BATTLE_005_ROUTE_102_TIANA.closure: Battle 5 is 10/10 because three young Pokémon and one true fossil create a complete snow puzzle without premature evolutions. Weather, Veil, two distinct Slush Rush attackers, priority, spread damage, and Bolt Beak make it severe, while every dependency has several independent answers.

registered_showcases: Ditto is the deliberately strange single-stage mirror opener.

competitive_references.adaptation: Ditto keeps the exact Choice Scarf and Imposter identity. Transform is its sole legal move; the copied opposing moves replace the empty slots immediately on entry.

Wimpod adapts Golisopod's Spikes, Aqua Jet, and automatic half-HP exit. Focus Sash, Taunt, and Leech Life let the fragile first stage contribute one tempo action without masquerading as its level-30 evolution.
Sandygast inherits Palossand's Water Compaction, Shore Up, Earth Power, Shadow Ball, and Toxic plan. Eviolite replaces Sitrus Berry to make the level-15 first stage a fair midfight anchor.

Tirtouga translates Carracosta's Solid Rock physical pressure to level 16. Weakness Policy makes super-effective hits an interactive risk, while Liquidation, Stone Edge, Aqua Jet, and Knock Off avoid another Shell Smash module.

BATTLE_006_ROUTE_104_BILLY.team_intent: Choice Scarf Imposter Ditto turns the player's chosen lead into the opening puzzle and explains Billy's strange tracks. Focus Sash Wimpod can Taunt or place one Spike before Wimp Out creates natural tempo; Eviolite Water Compaction Sandygast supplies recovery and status; level-16 Solid Rock Tirtouga is a reactive Weakness Policy ace with dual STAB, priority, and item removal rather than another setup move.
BATTLE_006_ROUTE_104_BILLY.intended_counterplay: Lead with a low-impact or status-focused Pokémon, exploit Ditto's Choice lock, or remove its Scarf. Taunt, multihit attacks, status, or immediate pressure limit Wimpod's one action. Special Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost, Dark, and Knock Off pressure Sandygast. Burn, Intimidate, Encore, item removal, safe neutral damage, or one decisive Grass attack avoids or answers Tirtouga's Weakness Policy. Ditto's variable type, Sandygast's Electric immunity, and Wimpod's Grass neutrality prevent one attack from solving the full sequence.
BATTLE_006_ROUTE_104_BILLY.bespoke_ai: Billy remains a deliberate singles pacing fight. Imposter and Wimp Out function automatically; normal foe-aware scoring understands the Choice lock, hazards, recovery, status, Weakness Policy, and priority, while smart switching escapes bad copies or matchups. The obsolete Tailwind speed-control profile is removed, and no move or turn is forced.
BATTLE_006_ROUTE_104_BILLY.uniqueness: Billy's footprint dialogue now describes a literal young shoreline mystery: a copied set of tracks, a fleeing beach bug, a living sand pile, and a fossil turtle from the cliffs. None appears in Battles 1-5; Sandygast and Tirtouga appear on no other current trainer, and Wimpod appears only once much later. The mature haunted shoreline quartet is preserved for a later ocean or abandoned-ship encounter.
BATTLE_006_ROUTE_104_BILLY.closure: Battle 6 is 10/10 because four low-stage or single-stage Pokémon create a variable mirror, tempo hazard, attrition anchor, and reactive ace without any premature evolution. Its difficulty comes from reading the sequence and managing items, not inflated final forms or a forced counter.

competitive_references.adaptation: Remoraid's Choice Scarf, Hustle, Water Spout, Seed Bomb, Fire Blast, and Hidden Power set is imported exactly. Its level-17 offset is safe because Remoraid does not evolve until 25.

Qwilfish keeps Sitrus Berry, Intimidate, Thunder Wave, Poison Jab, and Liquidation; Aqua Jet replaces Protect so the second-wave controller can also finish a weakened target.

Clamperl appears in zero corpus teams. Its Focus Sash Shell Smash, foe-only Muddy Water, Ice Beam, and Protect set is hand-authored because it is the stage-legal Fisherman payoff no mature ladder roster can supply.

BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN.team_intent: Level-17 Choice Scarf Remoraid and Expert Belt Dazzling Bruxish form the first cast: full-HP Water Spout attacks immediately while Dazzling blocks priority and Bruxish applies Taunt, screen breaking, and physical coverage. Sitrus Intimidate Qwilfish and level-16 Focus Sash Clamperl form the second cast: Thunder Wave and Intimidate buy one Shell Smash opportunity, then Muddy Water or Ice Beam converts it into pressure.
BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN.intended_counterplay: Any normal-speed hit weakens Water Spout; Storm Drain, Water Absorb, Dry Skin, Water resistance, Protect, Wide Guard where legal, or removing Remoraid's Scarf punish the first cast. Dazzling blocks priority but not ordinary attacks. Taunt, a double target, special pressure, Haze, Clear Smog, Trick Room, or phazing stops or reverses Clamperl; Grass and Electric attacks remain strong, while Qwilfish's Poison coverage and Clamperl's Ice Beam stop one-button sweeping. No exact capture or turn sequence is required.
BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN.bespoke_ai: Native doubles scoring understands Water Spout's HP scaling, Choice locking, Dazzling, Intimidate, Shell Smash, Muddy Water, Protect, and Thunder Wave. Darian adds HP awareness, smart switching, first-turn setup preference, and contextual speed control. Neither wave is scripted: Remoraid can change its Choice lock, Bruxish can attack or Taunt, and Clamperl's Smash remains interruptible.
BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN.uniqueness: Darian becomes Verdant's two-cast young-fish puzzle.
